Total parenteral nutrition. Safe administration and monitoring, step by step.

Step one. Know T P N: its indications, components and goals, why it is given by central or peripheral access, how it differs from enteral nutrition, and the patient's nutritional needs, planned with the dietitian, pharmacist and doctor.

Step two. Know the risks: metabolic, mechanical, and infectious. Watch for catheter related bloodstream infection, high blood glucose, and electrolyte imbalance. Interpret glucose, electrolytes and liver function tests, and start, adjust, and stop T P N according to protocol.

Step three. Prepare. Wash your hands and wear protective equipment. Introduce yourself, and identify the patient with the authorised identifiers. Explain the procedure and obtain verbal consent. Check the physician's order, organise the equipment, and prepare a sterile field.
Step four. Critical point. Compare the T P N label with the physician's order, and counter-check it with another staff member. Then stick the label on the bottle.

Step five. Critical point. Work as two. The assisting staff opens the IV set, syringes and needles, removes the bottle wrapping, and wipes it with an alcohol swab. The other nurse puts on gloves, and starts the infusion.

Step six. Critical point. Attach the T P N tubing to the central line port. Cover the ports with sterile gauze and tape them, then wrap the line limbs in a small green towel. Remove your gloves and position the patient comfortably.
Step seven. Set the infusion pump to deliver the prescribed volume. Dispose of the used equipment and wash your hands. Check the pump every hour.

Step eight. Critical point. Monitor vital signs every four to eight hours, blood glucose every six hours, and the central line site every shift. Give site care every forty eight hours, as per the infection control manual.
Step nine. Critical point. Never leave T P N solutions unattended. Put T P N and lipids on rolling infusion pumps, and encourage the patient to walk, if allowed.
Step ten. Keep strict sterile technique, watch for adverse reactions, work respectfully with the team, and educate the patient and family with empathy, protecting their dignity and privacy.

Step eleven. Document the prescription, administration times and rates, vital signs, fluid balance, and lab results. The electronic Kardex must be signed by two registered nurses. Weigh the patient daily, log intake and output, record the line status, and report any intolerance or complication immediately.
Watch, take the quiz, then get signed off.
